title: Restart Rates on Repayment Plans — Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery
content:
A restarted direct-payment repayment plan on a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** carries a restart rate on its monthly installment.

**Clause.** When a plan on the debt was approved before and a direct payment posted on the debt within the last calendar month counted back from today, the deposit restart rate of 105 percent applies. When a plan was approved before and no direct payment posted in that month, the no-deposit restart rate of 115 percent applies. When no plan was approved before, no restart rate applies.

A plan was approved before when a granted repayment plan decision is recorded on the debt. A direct payment falls in the last calendar month when less than one whole calendar month has passed from its posting date to today (on 20 October, 21 September counts and 20 September does not). Benefit offsets are not direct payments.

The restart rate is a percentage by which the quotient of the balance to be spread and the months is multiplied before the installment is rounded up to the cent.

| Earlier plan granted | Direct payment in the last calendar month | Restart rate |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 105 percent |
| Yes | No | 115 percent |
| No | Either | None |

**Hypothetical case.** A quotient of 150.00 USD on a debt whose earlier plan was granted and cancelled, with a direct payment posted nine days ago: 150.00 multiplied by 105 percent, that is 157.50 USD; with no payment that month, 172.50 USD.
